common: Close WaveForms before running a script; only one application can own the AD3.
Power off before changing wiring. AD3 GND, scope 1−, scope 2− and bench supply negative all connect to board GND. Never connect a ground clip to the negative rail.

Scope inputs: direct 1× flywires (default) or the BNC adapter with probes declared per channel by --probe, e.g. --probe 10,1 for a 10× probe on scope 1 and a 1× probe on scope 2; DC coupled, short ground returns. Each probe switch must match its channel setting. The digital and stack tests use only the two scope probes on header pins; the per-channel tests also use DIO inputs, which remain INPUTS and observe 0–5 V logic only.

Bench supply provides +5.00 V. Start with a 0.10 A current limit for standalone power/digital tests; 0.20 A for power + digital + one channel. These are conservative starting limits, not expected measured currents. If the supply remains in CC or a component heats, switch off and investigate; do not automatically raise the limit.

For digital, stack and channel fixtures without the Pi, provide +3.30 V at digital J2.3 from either a separate regulated bench channel OR AD3 V+ with --ad3-3v3. Never connect the two sources together. AD3 V− and W2 are unused. Never connect the Raspberry Pi during these tests; once it is connected, the Pi supplies the 3.3 V and AD3 V+ must be removed.
Scripts pause for connection changes and rail readings. They do not control or turn off the bench supply. Ctrl+C shuts down AD3 outputs; you must turn off the bench supply immediately afterwards.
order: Power standalone → digital standalone (two probe checks) → full stack without the Pi (rails, references, Pi-side clocks and data) → connect the Raspberry Pi. The per-channel tests exist for debugging a channel that misbehaves.

steps.title: Check AD3 pump stimulus before attaching it
steps.instructions: Keep W1 disconnected from the board. Connect scope 1+ to W1 and 1− to AD3 GND. The script generates 192 kHz, 0–5 V square wave on W1 and verifies it. W1 is then disabled before you attach the board.

steps.title: Power board supply and negative rail
steps.instructions: Power board only; no other boards. Connect bench +5 V to J3.2, bench return to J3.1, and W1 to J3.10. No digital board may drive PUMP at the same time. Turn on the bench supply only at the prompt; the script then starts W1. Let the pump settle.
steps.expect: +5 V: 4.75…5.25 V; negative rail: −5.25…−3.50 V. Gross ripple screen ≤150 mVpp over an 8 ms record, not a microvolt-noise measurement.

steps.title: Check both voltage references
steps.instructions: Keep the same supply and pump drive. Switch off the bench supply and let W1 stop at the prompt before moving the two scope leads.
steps.expect: VREF_P: 2.35…2.65 V; VREF_N: −2.65…−2.35 V; each within 3% of half the measured +5 V rail; ripple ≤150 mVpp.

steps.title: Digital board rails
steps.instructions: Digital board only; no power or channel boards. J1 shunt 1–2 selects the on-board 6.144 MHz crystal oscillator (U9/Y1); nothing connects to J2.7. Bench +5 V → J2.1 and GND → J2.2. Supply +3.3 V → J2.3 using the selected source. QL/QR are left open for this short test.

steps.title: Pi-side clocks: frequency and 3.3 V levels
steps.instructions: Power off; move only the two probe tips to the Pi header. These are the signals the Raspberry Pi will see, so both must be 3.3 V logic at the right frequency. Supplies stay as in the rails step.
steps.expect: PI_BCLK 3.072 MHz and PI_LRCLK 48 kHz, ±2%, 35–65% duty. Highs 2.7…3.6 V, lows −0.3…0.45 V. A high above 3.8 V fails; do not connect the Pi in that case.

steps.title: Bus clocks for the other boards
steps.instructions: Power off; move only the two probe tips to the bus header. MCLK feeds both channel modulators and PUMP drives the power board's charge pump.
steps.expect: MCLK 1.536 MHz and PUMP 192 kHz, ±2%, 35–65% duty, 5 V logic (highs 4.0…5.3 V). Together with the Pi-side pair this proves the crystal, the buffer and the whole divider chain.

steps.title: Check supplies under the channel load
steps.instructions: Connect ONLY the already-tested power and digital boards plus this one channel through correctly aligned bus connections. Bench +5 V goes to digital J2.1; +3.3 V to digital J2.3. Remove ALL temporary QL/QR-to-rail test jumpers left from the digital tests. Ground the unused channel bus input on DIGITAL ONLY if needed. The populated channel output must never be tied to a rail. W1 is disconnected for now.
steps.expect: Same +5 V and negative-rail screening windows, now with a real channel load.

steps.title: Reference voltages at the channel
steps.instructions: Power off before moving scope leads; keep the fixture otherwise unchanged.
steps.expect: Both references within their windows and within 3% of half +5 V.

steps.title: No-input modulator and feedback check
steps.instructions: With power off, short J20.1 to J20.2 (GND). Wire all DIO inputs below. RV20 must be fitted/wired; record its setting. Set J21 1–2 for left or 2–3 for right. DIO5 connects to J7.12 for left, or J7.14 for right to verify the selected bus output.
steps.expect: MCLK 1.536 MHz ±2%; Q must toggle with density 35–65%. QN and DACN complement Q; DACP and selected bus output follow Q (>99.5% settled agreement). This is a smoke test, not a noise-floor measurement.

steps.title: Two-level 1 kHz audio-response test
steps.instructions: Power off, remove the J20 input short, then connect W1 to J20.1 and AD3 GND to J20.2. Scope 1+ monitors J20.1; scope 2+ monitors J7.2. Keep DIO wiring. The script applies a zero-offset 1 kHz sine at 0.10 Vpeak, then 0.25 Vpeak; keep RV20 unchanged. It captures Q with MCLK, samples Q on falling clock edges, and averages groups of 256 bits.
steps.expect: Measured input amplitude within 20% of setting, with clean 1 kHz fit. Recovered density must contain 1 kHz (fit R² ≥0.25, density amplitude ≥0.003); larger input must produce 1.5…3.5× the smaller output amplitude. Absolute gain, THD, SNR and 24-bit performance are not certified.

steps.title: Check supplies under the channel load
steps.instructions: Connect ONLY the already-tested power and digital boards plus this one channel through correctly aligned bus connections. Bench +5 V goes to digital J2.1; +3.3 V to digital J2.3. Remove ALL temporary QL/QR-to-rail test jumpers left from the digital tests. Ground the unused channel bus input on DIGITAL ONLY if needed. The populated channel output must never be tied to a rail. W1 is disconnected for now.
steps.expect: Same +5 V and negative-rail screening windows, now with a real channel load.

steps.title: Reference voltages at the channel
steps.instructions: Power off before moving scope leads; keep the fixture otherwise unchanged.
steps.expect: Both references within their windows and within 3% of half +5 V.

steps.title: No-input modulator and feedback check
steps.instructions: With power off, short J20.1 to J20.2 (GND). Wire all DIO inputs below. RV20 must be fitted/wired; record its setting. Set J21 1–2 for left or 2–3 for right. DIO5 connects to J7.12 for left, or J7.14 for right to verify the selected bus output.

steps.instructions: Power off, remove the J20 input short, then connect W1 to J20.1 and AD3 GND to J20.2. Scope 1+ monitors J20.1; scope 2+ monitors J7.2. Keep DIO wiring. stack.title: Full stack, one channel at a time, without the Pi

steps.title: Rails with the left channel only
steps.instructions: Everything off. 1) Plug the LEFT channel board onto the power + digital stack using its 2×8 bus connector J7, so its pin 1 sits on pin 1 of the digital board's J4 and the power board's J3 (all three headers carry the same 16 signals). 2) On the left board put the J21 shunt on pins 1–2, the square-pad end. 3) Put a short wire between the two screw terminals of J20 (the LINE IN block) so the input is grounded. 4) Take the W1 coax off the power board: PUMP now comes from the digital board and two drivers must never share that pin. 5) Korad red → digital J2.1, Korad black → J2.2; the bus carries +5 V to the other boards. 6) AD3 V+ wire → digital J2.3. 7) Probe tips as listed below, ground clips on any bus GND pin. Korad current limit 0.20 A.
steps.expect: +5 V: 4.75…5.25 V; negative rail −5.25…−3.50 V with one channel loading it; gross ripple ≤150 mVpp. Persistent CC or heating: the channel board has a short; stop.

steps.title: Left modulator output on the bus
steps.instructions: Power off. Move only the two probe tips to the digital board's bus header J4: scope 1 on pin 12, scope 2 on pin 8. Nothing else changes.
steps.expect: MCLK 1.536 MHz. QL toggles (≥100 edges in the record) with a one-density of 35–65 % for a shorted input, at 5 V logic. Constant QL: the modulator is not running (check the channel's clock, ±5 V, references, flip-flop). Density far from 50 %: the input is not shorted or the integrator is stuck.

steps.title: Rails with both channels
steps.instructions: Power off. Plug the RIGHT channel board onto the stack the same way (J7 pin 1 on pin 1). On it: J21 shunt on pins 2–3, the end away from the square pad; a short wire across its J20 terminals. Move the probe tips back to power J3 pin 2 and pin 16. Raise the Korad current limit to 0.30 A.
steps.expect: +5 V: 4.75…5.25 V; negative rail −5.25…−3.50 V under the full load; gross ripple ≤150 mVpp.

steps.title: Right modulator output on the bus
steps.instructions: Power off. Move only scope 1's tip to J4 pin 14. Scope 2 stays on J4 pin 8.
steps.expect: Same as the left channel: toggling at 5 V logic, density 35–65 %.

steps.title: References under full load
steps.instructions: Power off. Move the two probe tips to power J3 pin 4 and pin 6. Both channels stay on the stack.
steps.expect: VREF_P 2.35…2.65 V, VREF_N −2.65…−2.35 V, each within 3% of half the measured +5 V.

steps.title: Pi-side clocks with the stack loaded
steps.instructions: Power off. Move the two probe tips to the digital board's Pi header J2: scope 1 on pin 4, scope 2 on pin 5.
steps.expect: Same windows as the standalone digital test: 3.072 MHz and 48 kHz at 3.3 V logic.

steps.title: Interleaved data reaching the Pi header
steps.instructions: Power off. Scope 1 tip to J2 pin 6, scope 2 tip to J2 pin 4. With both inputs shorted the two modulators idle around 50 % density, so PI_DIN must toggle continuously at 3.3 V logic.
steps.expect: PI_DIN toggles (≥100 edges in the record) with a one-density between 10% and 90% and 3.3 V logic levels; PI_BCLK 3.072 MHz. A constant PI_DIN means a stuck modulator, a wrong J21 selection or a dead bus line. This is a smoke test, not an audio measurement.
